avoid_supplements.name: Anticholinergic herbs (Jimson weed, henbane, deadly nightshade)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Additive anticholinergic effects leading to severe toxicity
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid completely; counsel patient on identification and avoidance

avoid_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
avoid_supplements.mechanism: CYP3A4 induction may decrease benztropine levels; reduced efficacy
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; consider alternative herbal supplements

avoid_supplements.name: Kava Kava
avoid_supplements.mechanism: May potentiate anticholinergic effects and increase CNS depression
avoid_supplements.action: Discontinue kava kava prior to benztropine initiation

caution_supplements.name: Ginseng
caution_supplements.mechanism: Potential mild anticholinergic properties; additive effects possible
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for excessive anticholinergic symptoms; use lowest effective dose

caution_supplements.name: Valerian
caution_supplements.mechanism: May increase sedation and CNS depression when combined
caution_supplements.action: Counsel on dizziness/drowsiness risk; avoid driving if combined

caution_foods.name: High-fiber foods
caution_foods.mechanism: Benztropine reduces GI motility; excessive fiber may worsen constipation
caution_foods.action: Moderate intake; ensure adequate hydration and monitor bowel function

caution_foods.name: Alcohol
caution_foods.mechanism: Additive CNS depression and anticholinergic effects
caution_foods.action: Limit alcohol consumption; counsel on increased drowsiness and impaired cognition

monitoring_notes: Monitor for anticholinergic toxicity signs (dry mouth, urinary retention, constipation, confusion, tachycardia) especially in elderly patients or those on multiple anticholinergic agents. Screen for drug interactions via CYP3A4 and CYP2D6 substrate/inhibitor medications.
